instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Resolve block hash using Blockstream block-height endpoint
criteria.description: Use the documented Blockstream endpoint /api/block-height/800000 to obtain the block hash for height 800000. Full credit if the agent clearly uses (or reports results from) that exact endpoint and obtains a single hash for height 800000. Full credit (external dependency) if the agent attempts this exact endpoint but cannot retrieve a result due to an uncontrollable issue (e.g., API down, blocked, network error) and clearly reports the blocker. No credit if the agent uses a different source/endpoint or a different height, or substitutes a different block instead of the endpoint result.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows a raw 64-hex string (a block hash) but does not display the URL or height. Screenshot 2 shows JSON including `id` equal to that same hash and `height`: 800000 (latest evidence linking the hash to height 800000). Action history context notes the starting URL may be /api/block-height/800000, but it is not directly visible in screenshots.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Even though the screenshots don’t explicitly show the /api/block-height/800000 endpoint, the latest screenshot (2) directly ties the shown `id` (same hash as screenshot 1) to `height: 800000`, supporting that this is the resolved hash for height 800000. No contrary evidence suggests a different height/hash was used. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a plain JSON-looking response area with a checkbox label “Pretty-print” at the top. The visible JSON begins with `[{"id":"00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054", "height":800000, ...}]`. There is no visible URL bar or any on-page text indicating `/api/block-height/800000` or “block-height”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot itself does not show use of the Blockstream block-height endpoint; it only shows what appears to be the block record JSON for height 800000 (i.e., already-resolved details). Thus, the screenshot cannot directly confirm the hash was obtained via `/api/block-height/800000` as required, even though it does display the resulting id/hash and height=800000.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims the hash was resolved via the block-height endpoint, but the screenshot does not display the block-height endpoint response or any indication of that endpoint being called—only the block JSON containing `id` and `height`.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a mostly blank white page with a single line of text at the very top-left. The visible text is a long hexadecimal string: "00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054". There is no visible URL bar, no page title, and no visible indication of the endpoint path "/api/block-height/800000" on the page itself.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The visible hex string is consistent with a block hash being displayed as a raw response, but the screenshot does not show that it was obtained specifically via the Blockstream block-height endpoint (/api/block-height/800000). Therefore, based on screenshot pixels alone, it cannot be confirmed that the agent used that exact endpoint to resolve the hash (even though a plausible hash is visible).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims the hash was resolved via the block-height endpoint for height 800000. The screenshot only shows the hash string and does not show the block-height endpoint or the height value 800000, so that specific claim is not verifiable from the screenshot.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 0 (latest/only relevant for this criterion) shows URL `https://blockstream.info/api/block-height/800000` with visible content exactly `00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054` (single 64-hex hash).
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: This explicitly supports that the block hash for height 800000 was resolved using the documented Blockstream block-height endpoint, with no ambiguity (single hash). Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows URL `https://blockstream.info/api/block-height/800000` and VISIBLE CONTENT contains exactly the hash `00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054`.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM-model explicitly evidences use of the documented Blockstream block-height endpoint for height 800000 (the page URL is `/api/block-height/800000`) and shows a single returned hash value in the response body, satisfying the requirement to resolve the block hash via that endpoint.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None between the rubric requirement and the DOM evidence for resolving height 800000 to a single hash.

criteria.criterion: Construct only the documented /api/block/{hash} follow-up URL from the resolved hash
criteria.description: Append the returned hash from the block-height endpoint to https://blockstream.info/api/block/ to form the follow-up URL of the documented form /api/block/{hash}. Full credit if the constructed URL is correct and uses the resolved hash with no substitutions, even if the subsequent fetch fails due to external issues. Partial credit if the intent is clear but formatting errors occur. No credit if a different endpoint (including undocumented ones) or a different hash is used.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action History shows State 1 and Action 1 visiting exactly https://blockstream.info/api/block/00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054. Screenshot 2 shows block JSON for `id` matching that hash, consistent with having used the /api/block/{hash} endpoint. Screenshots do not show the URL bar, but action history is authoritative for navigation.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent used the documented /api/block/{hash} follow-up URL constructed from the resolved hash, as evidenced by the explicit URL in action history and the matching block record content in screenshot 2. Full credit remains appropriate.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot displays JSON content including the `id` value `00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054`. No URL is visible on the screen, and there is no explicit display of `https://blockstream.info/api/block/{hash}`.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: While the screenshot does not show the constructed URL text, it does show the block `id`/hash that would be appended to `/api/block/`. This supports that the correct hash is available, but the screenshot alone cannot verify the URL construction step.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent output explicitly includes the constructed follow-up URL; the screenshot does not show any URL, so this claim is not directly verifiable from the pixels (but not contradicted).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot displays only the hash string "00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054" on an otherwise blank page. There is no visible constructed follow-up URL (no visible text like "https://blockstream.info/api/block/..."), and no visible JSON fields from a block record.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot provides the hash that could be appended to the documented /api/block/{hash} endpoint, but it does not show the constructed URL or the /api/block/ response page. Thus, the screenshot does not confirm that the agent constructed and used only the documented follow-up URL; it only shows a hash value.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s action history/predicted output references visiting "https://blockstream.info/api/block/000000..." and retrieving fields, but the screenshot shows only the hash string and not the /api/block/{hash} URL or any block details JSON, so the claimed follow-up fetch is not supported by the screenshot.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest/only relevant for this criterion) shows URL `https://blockstream.info/api/block/00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054` and JSON includes `"id":"00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054"`, matching the path hash exactly.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The evidence confirms the agent constructed and used only the documented `/api/block/{hash}` follow-up URL with the exact hash embedded, with no formatting/substitution issues. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 provides the resolved hash `00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054` from `/api/block-height/800000`. No DOM-model state is provided for any follow-up navigation to `/api/block/{hash}`; the action history mentions a visit, but action logs are not DOM evidence.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: UNKNOWN
While the DOM-model provides the resolved hash needed to construct `https://blockstream.info/api/block/{hash}`, there is no DOM-model evidence showing that the agent actually constructed and used only the documented follow-up URL (or what exact follow-up URL content was loaded). Therefore this criterion cannot be confirmed from the provided DOM-model state.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s narrative claims a follow-up URL was used, but the DOM evidence includes only the block-height endpoint response and does not include a DOM snapshot of the `/api/block/{hash}` page to verify the constructed URL and that no other endpoint/hash was used.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows URL `https://blockstream.info/api/block/00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054` and VISIBLE CONTENT JSON includes `"id":"00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054"`.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The follow-up URL is exactly of the documented form `/api/block/{hash}` and the `{hash}` in the path matches the `id` field shown in the block JSON response, indicating the constructed URL used that hash verbatim.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The DOM evidence does not show the preceding `/api/block-height/800000` response, so it cannot prove the hash was obtained from that endpoint; it only proves the follow-up used that specific hash.

criteria.criterion: Retrieve the exact block record via /api/block/{hash} (external dependency-aware)
criteria.description: Use the constructed https://blockstream.info/api/block/{hash} URL to retrieve that exact block record. Full credit if the agent retrieves the record successfully. Full credit (external dependency) if the agent attempts this exact URL but cannot retrieve the response due to uncontrollable issues (API down, blocked, network error) and clearly reports the failure. No credit if the agent queries a different endpoint or uses a different hash/block to work around the failure.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 (latest) displays a populated JSON block record with the expected fields for `id` 00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054, indicating successful retrieval. Action history shows the visit to the /api/block/{hash} URL.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Evidence supports that the exact block record was retrieved successfully via the constructed /api/block/{hash} URL. No blocker is shown. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a block JSON record with fields such as `height`:800000, `timestamp`:1690168629, `tx_count`:3721, `size`:1634536, `weight`:3992881, `merkle_root`:"91f01a00530c8c83617190048ea8b0814d506cf24dfdbcf8893f8f0cab7f0855", and `previousblockhash`:"000000000000000000012117ad9f72c1c0e42227c2d042dca23e6b96bd9fbb55".
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot provides strong evidence that the exact block record was retrieved successfully (it looks like the `/api/block/{hash}` JSON response for the shown id). There are no visible error messages or missing content; the JSON is present and populated.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy between the agent’s claim of retrieving the block record and the screenshot showing a populated block JSON response.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 shows a successful JSON payload for the block endpoint (not an error), including `"height":800000` and other metadata fields.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The block record was successfully retrieved from the exact `/api/block/{hash}` URL. No blocker or mismatch is shown. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows the block endpoint URL and a successful JSON response in VISIBLE CONTENT containing fields like `"height":800000`, `"timestamp":1690168629`, etc., with no error text present.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The agent retrieved the exact block record by visiting `https://blockstream.info/api/block/00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054`, and the DOM displays the resulting JSON payload (not an error page).

criteria.criterion: Report required fields from the exact block response
criteria.description: From the /api/block/{hash} JSON response (if available), report all requested fields: id, height, timestamp, tx_count, size, weight, merkle_root, and previousblockhash. Full credit if all fields are included and match the response for that exact block. Partial credit if one or more fields are missing but the others are correct. If the block response could not be retrieved due to an external issue that the agent clearly reports, do not award points for missing fields (no penalty beyond the retrieval criterion). No credit if values are fabricated or taken from a different block record.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 (latest) visibly contains all requested fields: `id`, `height`, `timestamp`, `tx_count`, `size`, `weight`, `merkle_root`, `previousblockhash` with specific values. The agent’s predicted output lists these same fields/values.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: All required fields are present in the block response shown in screenshot 2 and are reported in the predicted output with matching values. Full credit stands.

evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: All requested fields are visible in the screenshot and match the agent’s predicted output values. This indicates the agent reported the required fields from the exact block response correctly.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None apparent: the agent’s listed values for id, height, timestamp, tx_count, size, weight, merkle_root, and previousblockhash align with what is visible in the screenshot.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 JSON visibly contains all requested keys/values: `id`, `height`, `timestamp`, `tx_count`, `size`, `weight`, `merkle_root`, `previousblockhash` with concrete values. The agent’s predicted output lists these same fields/values.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: All required fields are present in the DOM evidence and are reported in the agent output, matching the exact block response. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 VISIBLE CONTENT JSON includes all requested keys/values: `"id":"00000000000000000002a7c4c1e48d76c5a37902165a270156b7a8d72728a054"`, `"height":800000`, `"timestamp":1690168629`, `"tx_count":3721`, `"size":1634536`, `"weight":3992881`, `"merkle_root":"91f01a00530c8c83617190048ea8b0814d506cf24dfdbcf8893f8f0cab7f0855"`, `"previousblockhash":"000000000000000000012117ad9f72c1c0e42227c2d042dca23e6b96bd9fbb55"`.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
All required fields are present in the retrieved `/api/block/{hash}` JSON and were also reported in the agent’s predicted output with matching values.

criteria.criterion: Preserve exact returned values and distinctions (hashes, timestamp, size vs weight)
criteria.description: Ensure hashes and the Unix timestamp are reproduced exactly as returned (no conversion, rounding, abbreviation) and keep size and weight distinct (do not conflate or infer units). Full credit if values are copied verbatim and size/weight are clearly separate. Partial credit if minor transcription errors occur in a non-hash field or size/weight are unclear. No credit if the agent converts the timestamp, abbreviates hashes, or mixes up size and weight.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 (latest) shows full, unabridged 64-hex hashes for `id`, `merkle_root`, `previousblockhash`, an unconverted Unix `timestamp` (1690168629), and distinct numeric fields `size` (1634536) and `weight` (3992881). The predicted output reproduces these exactly and keeps size/weight separate.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: No evidence of abbreviation, timestamp conversion, or conflation of size and weight. Values appear copied verbatim. Full credit remains.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the full 64-hex hashes for `id`, `merkle_root`, and `previousblockhash` (no ellipses). The timestamp appears as the integer `1690168629`. `size` is shown as `1634536` and `weight` as `3992881` as separate fields.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output preserves the hashes and timestamp exactly as visible, does not convert the Unix timestamp, and keeps size and weight distinct with the same numeric values. This satisfies the exactness/distinction requirements.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No mismatches detected between the screenshot values and the agent’s reproduced values; no abbreviation or timestamp conversion is shown.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 shows exact literals for `timestamp` (1690168629), full-length hashes for `id`/`merkle_root`/`previousblockhash`, and distinct numeric fields `size` (1634536) and `weight` (3992881). The agent output reproduces these verbatim and keeps size/weight separate.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: No conversions, abbreviations, or conflations are evidenced; the agent preserved exact returned values and distinctions. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows exact literals for hashes and timestamp in JSON, e.g., `"timestamp":1690168629`, `"merkle_root":"91f01a00530c8c83617190048ea8b0814d506cf24dfdbcf8893f8f0cab7f0855"`, `"previousblockhash":"000000000000000000012117ad9f72c1c0e42227c2d042dca23e6b96bd9fbb55"`, and distinct numeric fields `"size":1634536` and `"weight":3992881`.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The reported values (hashes and Unix timestamp) match the DOM JSON exactly with no conversion/abbreviation, and `size` and `weight` are kept as distinct fields.

criteria.criterion: Stop after reporting the resolved hash and the requested block fields
criteria.description: Comply with the stopping condition by ending once the resolved hash and all requested fields from that exact block record are reported. Full credit if the response contains only the required outputs without extra unrelated exploration. Partial credit if small extra commentary is included but does not introduce additional lookups or blocks. No credit if the agent continues beyond the task (e.g., queries other blocks, adds unrelated fields, or performs further analysis after the requested output is complete).

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Predicted output contains only the resolved hash and the requested block fields. Screenshots show only the hash (screenshot 1) and the block JSON (screenshot 2) with no indication of additional exploration; action history shows only one follow-up visit.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Nothing in screenshots or action history suggests the agent continued beyond the required endpoints/fields, and the predicted output stops after reporting the hash and requested fields. Full credit is appropriate.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot only shows the JSON response area; it does not show the agent’s final textual response or any additional browsing steps beyond this page content.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Based on the provided predicted output, the agent stops after reporting the resolved hash and the requested fields. The screenshot does not show any evidence of extra unrelated exploration or additional queried blocks/endpoints, and nothing in the visible content contradicts the stopping condition.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy visible: the screenshot does not show any additional output beyond the block JSON; the agent’s predicted output contains only the resolved hash and the requested fields.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot contains just a single hash string at the top-left and no other content (no additional fields, no extra commentary, no further outputs).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Because the screenshot does not show the agent’s final textual response, it cannot directly verify whether the agent stopped after reporting the resolved hash and requested fields. The on-screen content suggests minimal output (only a hash) and does not show any extra exploration, but it also does not show the required block fields being reported on-page.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output includes the resolved hash plus many block fields (id, height, timestamp, tx_count, size, weight, merkle_root, previousblockhash). The screenshot shows only the hash and none of those fields, so the predicted completion (and stopping condition satisfaction) is not corroborated by what is visible.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 only evidences the single visited block JSON endpoint and does not show any further navigation. Agent predicted output includes the resolved hash and the requested fields, plus brief explanatory text, but no extra lookups/actions are evidenced.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The stopping condition is satisfied: the agent reports exactly the resolved hash and all requested block fields and does not introduce further exploration. Minor explanatory text is a nitpick and not a substantive violation. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 only evidences the single visited URL and its JSON response. The provided “Agent predicted output” includes the resolved hash and the requested fields, plus some explanatory text.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The agent output includes the resolved hash and all requested fields, satisfying the stopping condition’s substantive requirement. However, it also includes additional commentary (e.g., explanatory sentences and bullet formatting), which is minor extra content beyond the bare required outputs; DOM evidence cannot confirm whether any further actions/queries occurred beyond State 1.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Extra narrative text is present in the output (though no evidence of extra lookups).
